thread:
maria: Quick sync — BigRetail wants a POC to run our streaming SDK with function calls + structured JSON output. They need 99th pct latency <150ms and ~80 QPS steady. Also asking about pricing for a 30-day trial and any enterprise blockers. cc @sam @elaine

sam: Got it. Do they plan to use Hosted or Dedicated for the POC? That changes pricing a lot.

maria: They prefer hosted initially, might go dedicated if throughput needs it. Security team flagged certs / onprem connectors — not sure yet.

elaine: For 80 qps streaming with short sequences, hosted can hit that if we enable continuous batching + prefix cache. Latency target is tight but doable with proper batch config and pinning a fast model variant.

sam: Pricing: for a 30-day eval at 80 qps sustained, I can sketch numbers but we should offer a short-term reserved capacity discount or credits. @dev-support can you draft a back-of-envelope?

dev-support: I can. Rough assumption: avg tokens per response 120, 80 qps -> ~9.6k tokens/s -> ~829M tokens/day. For hosted, estimate cost X/month — will DM exact calc. Also note streaming increases egress and connections.

maria: Security Q: they need mutual TLS for the webhook handshake and RBAC for callback endpoints. They also included a security questionnaire — attached in email. @li can you advise on cert + KMS requirements?

li: mTLS is supported for Private + Dedicated. For Hosted we support TLS + token auth; if customer needs mTLS we can provision a private connector or recommend Private. KMS: we integrate with AWS KMS / GCP KMS for key wrapping; HSM on contract. Ephemeral creds ok — we support short-lived tokens (15m TTL) and rotation endpoints.

elaine: Implementation note for streaming SDK + function calls: prefer SSE for this POC (simpler to firewall). If they want bi-directional low-latency, websocket works but handshake is trickier with corporate proxies. Structured output: we should use the tool-calling schema -> JSON schema enforcement on server side. Example snippet for the client:

```
const stream = client.stream({ model: 'fast-1', streaming: true, structured_schema: mySchema })
stream.on('data', (chunk) => { /* parse JSON objects */ })
```

sam: Also call out token rotation endpoint in the runbook. We had one customer hit 401s when their proxy cached old tokens.

maria: Are there known enterprise blockers for hosted here? Compliance, IP retention, audit logs, SLA?

li: Main blockers: (1) Data residency / logs (hosted keeps traces unless you opt out), (2) mTLS requirement, (3) legal SOW for cert handling. If they require full audit trail in their tenant, recommend Dedicated or Private. We can add audit log exports to SIEM via push.

elaine: Tech blocker: if they want function-call binary payloads + large attachments we need to confirm max payload size on their side and our proxy limits. For structured output, recommend schema + a small eval suite to catch regression.

sam: Suggest offering: 2-week staged POC: week1 - connectivity + handshake (tokens, certs), week2 - load/canary to validate 80 qps and latency. Offer $0 credits for week1 and 50% discounted reserved capacity for week2. Thoughts?

maria: Sounds good. Can you draft a short SOW bullet list for legal? I can attach to their SQ.

sam: Will do. SOW bullets: scope, duration, reserved capacity (if chosen), data handling, cert rotation policy, support hours, rollback plan.

dev-support: For the connectivity checklist:
- verify outbound ports (443) and websocket/SSE allowed
- if mTLS needed, exchange certs and test handshake
- token rotation endpoint: POST /v1/token/refresh -> returns short-lived token
- KMS wrap: provide key ARN for encrypting user data at rest

li: Also ask them to complete the section on endpoint ownership + SIEM integration. I'll prepare templated answers for the SQ.

elaine: Quick perf tip: use model variant `fast-1-quant` with our latency-optimized kernel. Set batching target to 6ms and max batch to 32 for best p99 vs throughput tradeoff. We'll instrument with per-route tracing.

maria: Who's owning the POC runbook and contact for on-call issues?

sam: I will own runbook + SOW. @elaine will own runtime config and perf validation. @li will own security questionnaire answers. @dev-support handles pricing calc and trial credit.

maria: Perfect. I'll reply to the customer with the staged plan and owners. Thanks all — please add any blockers in thread. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Deployment note: if we flip to Dedicated for week2, request submitted. ETA 48h after approval.

dev-support: Pricing estimate sent to @maria via DM (numbers, assumptions, and credit details).

li: SQ draft ready by EOD, I'll post link when done.

elaine: I'll prepare the perf test harness and a small prompt set for regression checks.

maria: Closing loop — I'll send calendar invite for kickoff tomorrow 11am. Thanks everyone.
